Built the Customers page as a `sheratan` module (replacing the earlier devices example scaffold):

- **`services/customers.contract.ts`** / **`customers.http.ts`** — `CustomerApi` contract and an HTTP adapter hitting `GET /api/customers`.
- **`modules/customers/`** — `customers.state.ts` (loading/ready/failed status), `customers.effects.ts` (a `resource()` with 3-attempt exponential-backoff retry, plus a `retry` intent that invalidates it), `customers.view.ts` (renders exactly one of `data-testid="loading"`, `data-testid="error"` + `data-testid="retry"`, or the table with `data-testid="customer-row"` rows), `customers.css`, `index.ts`, and state/effects tests.
- **`app.ts`** and **`styles/global.css`** updated to mount the customers module instead of the old devices example.

Verified: `tsc`, `oxlint`, `node --test`, and `sheratan check` all pass clean, and I drove the live app at `http://127.0.0.1:51826` with Playwright — confirmed the loading state appears, the table renders all 25 customers with correct columns, and (by forcing the API to fail) the error state with a working Retry button that recovers to the table, with only one of the three states visible at a time.

Done. The root cause was the automatic 3-attempt exponential-backoff retry I'd built into the `resource()` call — it made a single refusal silently retry (and sometimes succeed) before ever reaching the error state, and made "Retry" trigger its own multi-attempt cycle instead of exactly one request.

Fix: removed the `retry` option from `customers.effects.ts` — a refusal now reports immediately (one request), and the `retry` intent's `invalidate()` fires exactly one more request.

Verified:
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` (8/8, including new tests for these three behaviors), `npm run check` (sheratan: no violations) — all clean.
- Live-browser check against the running server with mocked network failures: refused load → exactly 1 request, error shown, zero rows, no loader; clicking Retry → exactly 1 more request, table appears, error/loader gone; state exclusivity held throughout.

It's done.
